external_source.provenance: real minted receipt from the Metrecept production signing path (src/at_utility/receipts.py::mint_receipt), demo key — kid does not resolve against the live directory; decoded payload is the fixture level
external_source.stranger_verification_path: scripts/verify_receipt.py against public JWKS (RFC 7638 kid thumbprint); verifier shipped independently three times (python script, python SDK receipt_check.py, browser-side TS port)

wire_format.transport: dual-emitted header X-Ohm-Receipt / X-Metrecept-Receipt (same value) on every served hit

field_semantics.tokens_replayed: served volume; provider tokens are 0 by construction on this hit shape (provider never called) — cost > 0 on zero provider-reported tokens is a first-class signed claim, not a logging edge case
field_semantics.meter_event_id: deliberately NOT request_sha256 — repeat hits on the byte-identical request produce distinct metered crossings, one per HTTP request, each with its own money identity
field_semantics.admit/plane/rl_epoch: provenance: admitted after dual-plane admission control; the edge never holds the signing key (edge-served hits are minted by the control plane during the edge-hit gate); bound to a UTC calendar day

limits.rule: The receipt signs pipe rent, not provider cost. pipe_usd is what the pipe billed for the crossing and never claims to be the provider invoice amount. Provider-cost assertions must come from provider-side columns, never from this payload.

estimated_provider_avoided_usd is NOT a receipt field: it lives in the usage ledger, is hit-only by design, and is unsigned, estimate-only, always labelled as such. A separate surface with a weaker trust posture — conflating it with the receipt overstates what the signature proves.

The receipt schema cannot express the request-3 shape. Provider prompt-cache hits (provider called, cache_read/cache_write on the invoice, discounted-but-nonzero) are invisible to the cache_hit kind: served / provider / billable as three independent counts must be modeled on the meter side for request-3.
iat is a claim, not a proof of time. The signature proves this key signed these bytes; the timestamp is another field in them. When-proofs are handled separately (Merkle clock over signature hashes).

request_sha256 is the digest of the canonicalized request: a semantically-identical-but-textually-different prompt is a different digest and a miss. tenant_sha256 is a truncated fingerprint — self-verifiable, not identifying.

observer_grade_mapping.signed_receipt_fields: settlement-grade (signature proves key signed bytes; L1/L3 bound the claim scope)
observer_grade_mapping.estimated_provider_avoided_usd: estimate-only, unsigned — self_attested class at best, hit-only by design (L2)
